body_markdown:
ChatGPT can generate code, but code alone is not an app. The gap between AI-generated snippets and a working, deployed application still requires databases, authentication, hosting, and deployment infrastructure. AI app builders can help close that gap by generating applications and, where supported, providing the infrastructure to deploy them on the web or mobile.


The demand for AI development tools continues to grow. According to the 2026 Developer Survey,[83% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) use at least one AI tool at work. However, a separate AI trust question found that[48% trust AI output](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-trust) when they can easily verify it. This gap between adoption and trust makes choosing the right app-building platform, with reliable infrastructure and opportunities for testing, increasingly important.


[Floot](https://floot.com/en) addresses this as a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides the managed infrastructure while the connected assistant handles development, within its available connector permissions. This list covers 12 options for turning AI-generated app ideas into real applications in 2027.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Managed Full-Stack Apps** :[Floot](https://floot.com/en) provides hosting, managed Postgres, authentication, and file storage for applications that need user accounts and saved data.
- **Floot's MCP Advantage** : The[Floot MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, letting users build through familiar AI tools.
- **Mobile App Publishing** : Floot supports[mobile app builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android, with monthly allowances on every plan. Store publishing requires separate developer accounts and approval.
- **Code and Data Ownership** : Floot users own their applications and data. The[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains database exports and paid-plan ZIP downloads.
- **Free to Start** : Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include 100 daily build actions and 2 monthly mobile builds on Free, with higher allowances and additional capabilities on paid plans.


## **What to Look For in an AI App Builder**


Turning ChatGPT-generated code into a deployed app requires more than a text editor. The platform needs to handle the services that make an application work in production. Before choosing a builder, evaluate its infrastructure, development workflow, deployment capabilities, code portability, and total running costs.


- **Code Ownership and Portability:** Check whether the code can be exported, synced with GitHub, and moved to another host if needed. Some platforms generate editable code with full ownership, while others keep the underlying code on their infrastructure.
- **Backend Services:** A production app typically needs a database, user authentication, file storage, and API endpoints. Evaluate whether the platform provides these services or requires separate configuration.
- **Deployment and Hosting:** Look for built-in hosting with SSL, custom domains, and production-ready infrastructure. Some platforms include hosting allowances in their plans, while others require external deployment.
- **Mobile App Capabilities:** If iOS or Android apps are needed, check whether the platform can package web apps for app stores or generate native mobile builds. Review developer-account requirements and submission workflows separately.
- **AI Assistant Integration:** Consider how interaction with the builder works. Some platforms use their own AI agents with separate billing. Others connect to existing AI assistants through MCP, with capabilities depending on the supported client and granted permissions.
- **Pricing Model:** Understand whether payment is per seat, per project, by usage, or through credits. Some platforms charge for AI interactions separately from hosting. Others have additional charges for database usage, storage, or mobile publishing.


## **1. Floot**


Floot operates as a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that integrates with supported AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol. It lets users[build and publish apps](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations without requiring a separate AI building subscription. The connected assistant handles development using available connector permissions, while Floot provides the managed infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot is designed for non-technical founders building MVPs, small business owners needing custom internal tools, and freelancers serving clients. The platform handles TypeScript and React projects with[managed Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , user authentication, file storage, email and push notifications, payments, and usage-billed hosting.


Its full-stack infrastructure supports applications that require persistent data, user accounts, backend operations, and deployment without manually configuring several services.


### **Key Capabilities**


- MCP connector for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Codex
- Managed PostgreSQL databases with browser-based table view
- Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without separate OAuth app setup
- [Mobile app conversion](https://floot.com/en/mobile) for iOS and Android with monthly build allowances
- Code and data ownership on every plan; full project ZIP export requires a paid plan
- SEO controls with server-side pre-rendering for crawlers


### **Why It Leads**


Floot is free to start. According to its[current pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , the Free plan provides 100 build actions per day, 2 mobile app builds per month, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year.


Pro costs $25 per month with 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, custom domains, 12 mobile builds, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Power costs $100 per month with 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, unlimited mobile builds, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance. Annual billing provides two months free.


Hosting beyond the allowances is usage-billed. Building through a supported connected AI assistant uses the user's eligible AI subscription rather than Floot AI build credits. Floot AI credits apply to optional features such as its own agent, image generation, and AI inside published apps. The platform is backed by Y Combinator.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is a full-stack AI web app builder that generates React and TanStack Start projects with backend services. In August 2026, Lovable reported more than 60 million projects and over 900 million monthly visits to apps built on its platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable works well for non-technical founders testing ideas or building MVPs. The platform emphasizes chat-driven development with two-way GitHub synchronization and managed backend services through Lovable Cloud.


It suits teams that prefer building inside a dedicated AI application interface while retaining access to their generated code through GitHub.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Chat-driven full-stack development
- Two-way GitHub synchronization
- Lovable Cloud for backend services
- Automatic basic security scans on publishing, with deeper scans available on demand
- Growth tools including SEO review, Google/Meta ads, and landing pages


### **Considerations**


The Pro plan costs $25 per month with 100 monthly credits. The platform has documented customer success stories including enterprise cost savings.


Teams should evaluate how monthly credits, hosting usage, and integrations affect their overall development costs. For a comparison of development workflows and billing models, see[Floot vs Lovable](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) .


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI coding agent that handles full-stack code generation with intelligent model routing. Bolt advertises automated testing and refactoring, though its error-reduction claims are vendor-reported rather than independently verified.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt works for teams that want a balance between AI assistance and hands-on code control. On Teams and Enterprise plans, it supports importing custom design systems from GitHub, npm registries, and Storybook to maintain brand consistency.


This approach can suit teams working with established interface components and development conventions across multiple projects.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Full-stack code generation in browser
- Bolt Cloud hosting with databases
- Custom design system imports on Teams and Enterprise plans
- Automatic testing and refactoring
- MCP-based connectors for accessing external tools


### **Considerations**


The Free plan includes 1 million tokens per month. Pro costs $25 per month with 10 million tokens. Teams should evaluate how the token-based model aligns with their expected usage.


Bolt supports hosted projects and backend functionality. Its workflow differs from platforms that let an existing AI assistant directly manage external app infrastructure. See the[Floot vs Bolt](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) comparison for more context.


## **4. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent is a cloud development environment with AI-assisted coding, built-in services, and collaborative features. The platform supports non-technical builders as well as developers who want direct access to the underlying code.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit fits organizations that need a full development environment alongside AI assistance. It includes development and production database separation, which supports more structured deployment workflows.


The platform is particularly relevant when multiple contributors need to inspect, test, and modify application code within a shared environment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Built-in authentication, database, hosting, and monitoring
- 100+ integrations including OpenAI, Stripe, and Google Workspace
- Intelligent model routing with Free, Power, and Max modes
- Up to 15 collaborators and 50 viewers on Pro plan
- Infinite Canvas for visual design exploration


### **Considerations**


Core plans cost $20 per month while Pro plans cost $100 per month on monthly billing. The platform serves enterprise customers including Databricks, Zillow, and Gusto.


Replit's AI-assisted development environment and usage-based features should be evaluated alongside deployment requirements. The[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) comparison explains differences in infrastructure management and AI billing.


## **5. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is an AI code generator focused on Next.js and React applications with one-click deployment to Vercel infrastructure.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 works well for teams already using Vercel and Next.js. It generates full-stack applications with GitHub sync and pull request workflows that integrate into existing development processes.


The platform is suitable for teams that want AI-generated application code while maintaining development workflows centered on GitHub and Vercel hosting.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Full-stack Next.js application generation
- One-click deployment to Vercel
- GitHub sync and pull requests
- Design Mode for visual layout adjustments
- Security-first approach with explicit code review recommendations


### **Considerations**


The Free tier includes access to v0 and deployment features, with usage limits. Plus plans cost $30 per user per month while Business plans cost $100 per user per month.


Per-user pricing may add up for larger teams. Applications requiring databases, authentication, or specialized backend services may also involve infrastructure configuration and costs through the Vercel ecosystem.


## **6. Base44**


Base44 is a prompt-based app builder with built-in marketing tools. Wix acquired the company in June 2025, adding enterprise backing to the platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 suits teams that want app building combined with post-launch marketing capabilities. The platform includes Google Ads, social posts, and GEO features alongside standard app development.


Its integrated development and marketing approach is suitable for founders and businesses that want to create applications and manage related promotional activities from one platform.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Built-in authentication, database, and analytics on every plan
- Two-way GitHub sync available on Builder and higher plans
- Security scan with one-click fixes
- Marketing tools including ads and social integration
- Source-code export options for paid users


### **Considerations**


Starter plans cost $16 per month on annual billing, Builder plans $40 per month, and Pro plans $80 per month.


The platform uses message and integration credits for various activities. Teams should evaluate the credit allowances and supported integrations when estimating ongoing costs for application development and operation.


## **7. Softr**


Softr builds apps from components with a database and app-building environment together, minimizing generated code that needs maintenance. The platform added MCP integration for Claude and ChatGPT in 2026, with an official connector announcement in October.


### **Organizational Fit**


Softr works well for operations teams building internal tools with complex user permissions. Its app-user pricing model differs from per-seat approaches common in other platforms.


The platform supports teams that need configurable access controls and applications connected to existing business data sources.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Component-based building with no generated code to maintain
- User groups and permissions system
- SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance with data hosting options in Germany
- Integrations with Airtable, HubSpot, SQL databases, Google Sheets, and Notion
- Visual editing and MCP-based building without consuming Softr AI credits


### **Considerations**


Free plans are available. Basic plans cost $19 per month, Pro $99 per month, and Business $329 per month on annual billing.


The platform prioritizes compliance and data residency controls. Teams should examine app-user allowances, permissions, and connected data sources when selecting a subscription for internal business applications.


## **8. Bubble**


Bubble is a visual no-code platform with an AI agent that drafts pages and logic. The platform supports native iOS and Android app publishing to app stores.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble suits teams that want extensive design flexibility and native mobile publishing. Its visual editor provides detailed control over application layouts and workflows.


The platform works for users who prefer configuring application behavior through visual interfaces rather than primarily relying on generated source code.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Visual editor for web apps and native iOS/Android
- AI agent for page and logic drafting
- One-click deployment
- SOC 2 Type II compliant infrastructure
- Workload-unit-based hosting and capacity management


### **Considerations**


Free plans support development only. Web-only Starter costs $32 per month, Growth $119 per month, and Team $349 per month on annual billing. Separate Mobile and Web & Mobile plans have different prices.


Bubble's MCP beta lets compatible AI assistants work with Bubble applications, but the platform does not provide runnable source-code export.


Teams comparing visual app development with AI-assisted full-stack development can review[Floot vs Bubble](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bubble-which-no-code-platform-is-right-for-you-in-2026) .


## **9. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create and host websites directly from ChatGPT conversations. Sites hosting is currently included with eligible ChatGPT plans, but building and editing Sites consumes Codex usage, and hosting and storage limits still apply.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites provides a convenient entry point for users already working in ChatGPT. Eligible users can build, preview, and publish websites or lightweight applications without setting up a separate hosting account.


The platform is suited to dashboards, information portals, and applications that fit its supported runtime and infrastructure limits.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Website creation from ChatGPT conversations
- Built-in storage and database capabilities
- Sign in with ChatGPT credentials
- Collaborative editing
- Custom domains where supported


### **Considerations**


Supported runtime, integrations, and hosting limits vary by ChatGPT account type. The platform works well for lightweight applications.


Apps requiring unsupported frameworks, specialized backend services, or more complex infrastructure may need additional services or a dedicated full-stack platform.


## **10. GlideOS**


GlideOS is an AI software development platform that turns spreadsheets, documents, and natural-language prompts into business applications. It is separate from Glide Classic, the company's original visual no-code platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


GlideOS works well for field teams and internal business tools. Its spreadsheet-based starting point suits organizations that already manage operational data in files or connected data sources.


Teams can also begin from a written description and use an AI agent to create and refine application interfaces and workflows.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Spreadsheet-to-app conversion
- AI-assisted app creation through natural-language prompts
- Internal business applications across desktop and mobile devices
- Written briefs, screenshots, and PDFs as input
- Agent-based interface and workflow development


### **Considerations**


Free plans have limited credits. Basic costs $25 per month, Plus $50 per month, and Pro starts at $125 per month. The plans provide different allowances for published applications, workflows, users, and AI credits.


GlideOS operates separately from Glide Classic, with its own subscriptions and project environment. Teams using older Glide applications should account for this distinction when evaluating migration or new development.


## **11. Cursor**


Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built as a fork of VS Code. It supports multi-agent systems for planning, coding, and testing simultaneously.


### **Organizational Fit**


Cursor fits developers who want to stay in a familiar IDE while using AI assistance. The platform can connect to[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) for managed backend infrastructure.


This makes Cursor relevant to developers who want direct code control while using a separate provider for databases, authentication, hosting, and deployment.


### **Key Capabilities**


- AI-first IDE based on VS Code
- Multi-agent system for concurrent tasks
- Visual debugging with screenshots and recordings
- Browser-based app verification
- Integration with external infrastructure providers


### **Considerations**


Cursor is a code editor rather than a complete managed app infrastructure platform. Teams typically pair it with hosting and backend infrastructure from another provider.


This combination offers extensive code control with managed services. Cursor and Floot can therefore work together instead of serving as direct substitutes for the same development functions.


## **12. Google AI Studio**


Google AI Studio supports vibe coding for web apps with a React frontend and Node.js server, plus native Android app generation.


### **Organizational Fit**


Google AI Studio suits teams prototyping AI-powered apps with Gemini integration. The platform provides native access to Google's AI capabilities within the development workflow.


It is suitable for users building web applications or experimenting with Android development through a browser-based environment and integrated AI tools.


### **Key Capabilities**


- Web app generation with React and Node.js
- Native Android app generation
- GitHub import capability
- Native Gemini AI integration
- Google Cloud infrastructure


### **Considerations**


Google AI Studio lets new users deploy their first two apps to Google Cloud at no cost. Further deployments and resource usage may incur Google Cloud charges.


Availability and publishing requirements vary by account and application type. Users should also distinguish between web deployment and native Android publishing, which can involve separate account and testing requirements.


## **How Floot Turns ChatGPT Ideas Into Deployed Apps**


The core challenge with AI-generated code is moving from a working snippet to a deployed application.[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) addresses this by connecting supported AI assistants to managed application infrastructure. Users can build, edit, test, and publish through their existing assistant, with available actions depending on its connector permissions.


Floot simplifies the process through three capabilities:


- **Existing AI Subscriptions:** Supported assistants handle development through the user's own AI subscription, avoiding separate Floot AI build-credit charges. Floot plan limits, hosting costs, and optional AI-feature charges still apply.
- **Managed Infrastructure:**[Floot provides Postgres](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, backend endpoints, file storage, email, payments, and hosting without requiring users to configure separate infrastructure services.
- **Mobile Publishing:**[Floot supports mobile builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) for iOS and Android without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio installations. Publishing requires developer accounts and store approval.


For non-technical founders and business owners, Floot provides a path from an AI conversation to a deployed application with persistent data, authentication, and managed hosting.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can a complete app be built using ChatGPT-generated code without any coding experience?**


Yes. ChatGPT can generate frontend components, API logic, and database schemas, while compatible app-building platforms provide infrastructure and deployment capabilities. With[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , supported ChatGPT configurations can create, edit, and publish applications through a Floot project. Floot handles managed databases, authentication, and hosting. Available development actions depend on the connected AI client's permissions and supported tools.


### **What are the typical costs associated with using an AI app builder for a production app?**


Paid AI app builder plans vary by provider, usage model, and deployment requirements.[Floot Pro](https://floot.com/en/pricing) costs $25 per month with 1,000 daily build actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Additional hosting beyond the allowance is usage-billed. Building through a supported connected AI assistant uses its separate subscription. Mobile app store submissions require an Apple Developer Program membership ($99 per year) and a Google Play developer account ($25 one-time).


### **How do AI app builders handle database management and user authentication?**


Platforms vary significantly in their database and authentication services. Floot provides managed Postgres with SQL access and a browser-based table view, plus Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without separate OAuth app registration. Other platforms may provide integrated backend services or require external configuration. Users should check whether authentication, database management, data exports, and backup options are included in their selected plans.


### **What are the limitations of using a free AI app builder, and when should an upgrade happen?**


Free plans often limit usage, mobile app builds, or features like custom domains. Floot's Free plan includes 100 daily build actions with no weekly cap, 2 mobile builds per month, and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year. Upgrade when custom domains, higher action limits, scheduled jobs running in published apps, or additional mobile builds are needed. Hosting beyond available credits requires additional payment.


### **Can an app built with an AI app builder be published to the Apple App Store or Google Play Store?**


Yes, though publishing requirements vary by platform.[Floot's mobile workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) packages web applications into iOS and Android builds and supports delivery to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks. Separate Apple Developer and Google Play developer accounts are required. Apple account connections are available on every Floot plan, while connecting Google Play requires a paid plan. Final store approval depends on each store's review guidelines.
